mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, leading to decreased corporate borrowing and investment, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in >60% of cases with high FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive when UNRATE rises, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive with slow GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive despite declining INDPRO, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) slows but employment (PAYEMS) rises, inefficiency may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive when GDPC1 slows but PAYEMS rises, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High FEDFUNDS with rising CPIAUCSL may signal stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive under these conditions, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST) indicate economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive with declining HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative with rising PAYEMS, the hypothesis fails.
